prize_parts.citation: for the development of general palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: I have changed my preferred configuration from the two-part B057 plus B058 prize to B057 alone, credited to Buchwald and Hartwig. The reasons are scientific, not a count of hands. Palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling has a clear principle (ligand control of the amido-palladium reductive elimination step), a quantitative mechanistic basis that guides ligand design, about three decades of independent confirmation, and routine use at scale in process chemistry. It is the one candidate on which nobody in round 1 disputes maturity or the credited pair. The remaining questions are the 2010 overlap and the Kosugi/Migita precursor, and both can be handled in the citation wording: the formation of C-N bonds from aryl halides and amines through ligand design is a different bond-forming problem from the C-C couplings honored in 2010, and the word 'general' states what the 1983 tin-amide reaction, which needed stoichiometric organotin amides and had narrow scope, did not deliver. I cannot judge the synthetic literature as an expert, so I rely on the specialists here, but their statements converge on this point.
statement.case_against: A single method prize is narrower in conceptual reach than degradation or base editing, and a colleague may fairly call it a second chapter of the palladium cross-coupling story. Dropping base editing also discards what I still regard as the most genuinely new capability on the shortlist, and a Buchwald-Hartwig citation does not formally resolve Kosugi's priority; it only words around it. If the committee finds the 2010 overlap decisive, this configuration has no obvious fallback among the contested alternatives.

responses.point: Base editing fuses known deaminases to a Cas protein, so the chemical step is existing deamination chemistry and the novelty lies mainly in protein engineering and directed evolution; closeness to the 2020 prize and trainee credit add caution.
responses.response: This is the argument that moved me most. I had defended B058 as a new chemical capability, but if the reaction itself is known deamination and the new element is engineering of the delivery and specificity, then it is a weaker chemistry citation than a new catalytic method, and I cannot give a citation that would be read as protein engineering with a chemical label. I accept your reading and have removed B058 from my preferred configuration. I also thank you for the clear statement that the C-N problem differs from C-C coupling, which I use in the B057 wording.

responses.point: C-N coupling is chemically distinct from the 2010 prize (a different bond type and a ligand problem for reductive elimination from amido complexes), though Kosugi and Migita remain a precursor a purist cannot dismiss.
responses.response: I adopt your distinction as the answer to my own question on overlap: the 2010 citation concerned C-C bond formation, and the difficulty here was making reductive elimination from palladium amido complexes work with a general ligand design. On Kosugi, I do not think a third name is justified unless the expert record shows the 1983 chemistry was already general and catalytic in the practical sense; I read your reservation as a request for that evidence, and I would rather state 'general' in the citation than add a name by default. You also asked whether a Liu-only base editing credit is defensible: I think it is, but your doubt about chemistry versus genome engineering is enough that I no longer press it.

responses.point: B057's maturity does not by itself outweigh a new design principle; targeted protein degradation is event-driven, reaches undruggable proteins and has a clear transferable rule, with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as the cleanest trio.
responses.response: I agree that induced proximity is a real design principle and I keep B004 as an alternative. Where I differ is on readiness for this year's citation: you and Chabes both say the PROTAC and cereblon-glue strands are two discoveries that three names cannot cover, and no PROTAC drug is approved. A prize that omits Handa and Ito for the glue lineage, or Crews and Deshaies for the concept, would draw the under-crediting criticism you describe yourself. I would revisit B004 once the committee can state one induced-proximity citation and a defensible name set; today that is not settled.

responses.point: Kosugi and Migita's priority is a real attribution complication, and for base editing Liu's conceptual leadership should be separated from the Komor, Gaudelli and Nishida-Kondo strands before supporting it.
responses.response: I accept your point on priority, and I want the expert record to separate the 1983 tin-amide coupling from the ligand-enabled catalytic systems in concrete terms of scope and catalytic turnover rather than leave it to the citation adjective. On base editing, your demand for evidence that the trainees conceived and did not only execute the work is not met in the record before us, and that, with Nishida and Kondo's independent 2016 route, is a further reason I withdrew it from my configuration. I would not rank your B026 above B057 either, since the added distinction beyond the 1992 Marcus prize and the Dutton-Moser and Beratan-Onuchic parallel claims that you yourself raise remain open.

responses.point: B004 is the most coherent subset of Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, but it is really two discoveries (PROTACs and molecular glues), and B057 or B058 are cleaner on attribution if the credit split is too contested.
responses.response: Your own statement that B057 and B058 are cleaner on attribution is the reason I now treat B057 as the more defensible single citation. I take your weight on two decades of degrader replication seriously, and I accept that deaminase enzymology is the kind of reaction-level insight you value, but a configuration for B004 needs the committee to settle whether glues and PROTACs are one achievement before we can write names that survive scrutiny. I remain open to B004 or B058 as a second part only if a name set fits within the three-person cap, which with B057's two names would leave room for one person only.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that C-N coupling is distinct enough from the 2010 cross-coupling prize, which I now rely on the chemists' argument to settle
Whether Kosugi and Migita's 1983 tin-amide work was general enough to warrant a name; I assume it was not, but cannot verify this myself
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug and the unsettled credit split make B004 premature this year or only premature relative to B057
Whether base editing, which I still consider a significant new capability, will look more clearly chemical, and mature in safety data, in a later year
Whether a single-part prize leaves the committee without the breadth of a two-part prize that some members may prefer
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate. I shared a Lund University affiliation with Somfai and Sparr, which is not a conflict with any candidate. I am a physicist rather than a synthetic chemist and have no personal or collaborative link to Buchwald, Hartwig, Liu or any other named candidate. No change from round 1.
